editorial.headline: Technical Inspection Services: Foreign-Open, Not Moratorium-Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers on-site physical, visual and technical inspections, open to every business scale and to full foreign ownership nationally.
editorial.body:
Technical Inspection Services is the on-site work of examining products, facilities, services or processes—physically, visually or through technical methods—to assess compliance with standards, specifications or regulations. Its scope is broad but coherent: agricultural processes and inspections; fisheries assessments and compliance inspections; health-facility infrastructure; technical traceability for exports, imports and inter-island trade; and inspections in infrastructure, manufacturing and safety. It also includes visual inspection, periodic inspection services, installation-inspection services, ship-classification inspection, aerodrome-safety inspection and inspection of health facilities and infrastructure.

The practical common thread is verification at the point where an activity, asset or product can be observed and tested. That can mean inspection connected with oil and gas, electricity, disaster-protection facilities, non-destructive testing, commercial buildings and their environmental setting, including exhaust emissions, ambient-air quality and working environments. It can also concern manufactured goods such as food and beverages, pharmaceuticals, textiles and textile products, production processes and children’s toys. The code is therefore suited to an inspection operation whose stated work is assessing conformity in the field, rather than merely advising on it.

At Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale, registration is open. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA and permits foreign ownership up to 100%. That is a direct reading: a foreign investor may register this technical-inspection activity under the national position without a foreign-equity cap below full ownership.

Bali does not reverse that national opening. The provincial rule blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the island on a permanent basis. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At Besar scale, the OSS risk reading is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which is why the activity sits outside the moratorium block rather than within it. For a foreign-owned registration in Bali, the honest conclusion is straightforward: this activity is not moratorium-blocked, while the Besar-scale risk classification remains Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi.
